title: LyraForge - Marketplace listing, KMS & LLM routing design review
summary: Deep technical sync to finalize marketplace listing requirements, KMS/HSM compatibility, and LLM routing/fallback patterns for LyraForge joint solution. Reviewed VPC connector, audit log requirements, quantization tradeoffs, and pilot plan for perf benching.
topics: VPC connector networking and firewall rules
LLM routing policy: latency vs cost fallbacks
next_steps: Redwood to share marketplace packaging checklist and sample helm chart link
LyraForge to provide test KMS credentials (scoped) and sample artifact storage location
Schedule 2-hour perf lab on Apr 6 for quant+latency benchmarks
SE to draft routing policy matrix and canary plan
Exchange SOC2 and encryption docs via secure link
action_items: Marco Chen: produce VPC connector runbook draft by 2027-03-22
Sofia Martinez: validate LyraForge KMS policy and send example IAM role by 2027-03-19
Jasmine Rowe: send pricing/commit options and sample listing metadata by 2027-03-18
Owen Brooks: provide sample request distribution (QPS, 95th latency targets) by 2027-03-20
transcript:
Meeting header: 2027-03-14 15:30 PDT — Duration 58m; Recording on. Attendees listed above.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Jasmine): hey everyone thanks for joining on a friday afternoon, appreciate it. quick agenda — marketplace listing reqs, kms/hsm compatibility, networking, and then routing fallbacks. is that right, nadia?
00:18 Speaker 2 (Nadia): yep that looks good. we have Sofia and Owen on to answer the infra bits. we also wanted to make sure audit logs and key rotation fit our compliance program.
00:30 Speaker 3 (Marco): cool — i'll start with the VPC connector and packaging. real quick caveat: our connector expects three outbound ports, 443 plus ephemeral for healthcheck, and a nat egress. some customers put in weird firewall rules so we wanted to call that out.
00:48 Speaker 4 (Owen): oh yeah we run pretty tight egress policies. is there a documented list of ip ranges or a static egress address for the hosted listing?
01:00 Speaker 3 (Marco): ah, good q — for the marketplace listing, when deployed as "Private (VPC)" mode, the control plane can be customer-managed in VPC peering and we provide static egress ranges per region. i'll attach the ip-range doc but for initial lab we'll give you a scoped allowlist.
01:18 Speaker 4 (Owen): perfect, that'll help firewall rule changes.
01:24 Speaker 5 (Sofia): about KMS — we need to ensure keys never leave our HSM, and rotation is automated. do you support bring-your-own-kms with grpc based key wrapping?
01:36 Speaker 3 (Marco): yes, we support BYOK with KMIP and cloud KMS providers; for HSM-backed flows we do envelope encryption: customer key wraps the model artifacts and we never persist plaintext. small caveat: in certain canary flows we need to persist encrypted inference cache metadata — that's redactable.
01:58 Speaker 2 (Nadia): can you explain the canary flow bit? we want to ensure no plaintext or unencrypted caches in any Redwood-managed buckets.
02:08 Speaker 3 (Marco): sure. by canary i mean: when you rollout a model variant we keep some prefix KV cache to warm subsequent requests. that cache can be encrypted with your key, but there are edgecases where we fallback to a shared cache for latency sensitive paths. we recommend pinned dedicated capacity if you need absolute data isolation.
02:32 Speaker 5 (Sofia): pinned dedicated capacity is likely what we need for first phase. can you give SLA numbers for that?
02:40 Speaker 1 (Jasmine): dedicated capacity SLA is 99.95 for availability and steady-state 95th token latency targets are in the perf profile; i'll send the SLA doc.
02:52 Speaker 6 (Ethan): quick question on quantization — we plan to use a 4-bit quantized model to reduce cost. does Redwood's runtime support the quant bits we plan to use and how does that impact throughput?
03:04 Speaker 3 (Marco): we support int4 and several mixed-precision paths. throughput improves, but there's a small hit on quality for some instruction-following tasks. for routing we can route lower-criticality traffic to the quantized variant, and high-criticality to fp16 or bfloat16 variant.
03:28 Speaker 2 (Nadia): so we need a routing policy that considers latency SLO, cost per token, and quality threshold. do you have a matrix for that?
03:40 Speaker 7 (Priya): yes, we have a routing policy matrix template. it maps traffic buckets by intent/priority to model variants and includes fallback timing. we can customize thresholds — Marco will produce an initial draft.
03:54 Speaker 3 (Marco): i'll put together a policy doc that outlines canary percentage, time windows, and automatic fallback to the last known-good model if errors spike.
04:06 Speaker 6 (Ethan): great. on telemetry — we need per-request tracing tied to our request id and retention for 90 days for debugging. can you push traces to our OTLP endpoint?
04:18 Speaker 3 (Marco): yes, we can forward traces and logs to a customer OTLP collector in VPC mode; for hosted we offer anonymized token-level breakdowns but PII must be redacted. we'll show the tracing hook in the runbook.
04:34 Speaker 4 (Owen): for the marketplace listing itself — packaging wise, do you require a helm chart plus a listing manifest?
04:42 Speaker 1 (Jasmine): typically we ask partners to submit a packaging bundle: helm chart (or operator), listing metadata (yaml), and a runbook. we'll share a sample repo link.
04:52 Speaker 2 (Nadia): can you also support a managed-on-our-account model for initial beta before we move to BYOK?
05:02 Speaker 1 (Jasmine): yes, we can do a managed pilot with strict contract: ephemeral keys, no cross-tenant caching, and contractually enforced retention windows. handoff to BYOK later is supported.
05:14 Speaker 5 (Sofia): audit logs — we require immutable audit trail for all encryption key operations and admin actions. is there an integration for SIEM ingestion?
05:26 Speaker 3 (Marco): we push audit logs to S3 or to an external syslog/siem via forwarder. logs are signable and we support retention policies. i'll include example event schemas.
05:38 Speaker 7 (Priya): also, when listing to marketplace, we need to publish a small reference architecture doc that shows network flow — we can co-author that with your docs team.
05:50 Speaker 2 (Nadia): yes please, a diagram with the VPC peering, subnets, and KMS flow would be ideal.
06:00 Speaker 3 (Marco): noted.
06:06 Speaker 5 (Sofia): one more on encryption: if we rotate keys every 30 days, will that impact cached embeddings and require rewarming?
06:18 Speaker 3 (Marco): rotation triggers a re-encryption step for stored artifacts; for live caches we have a lazy rewrap that doesn't block serving, but you'll see a small latency blip. we can schedule rotations during low traffic windows.
06:34 Speaker 6 (Ethan): about benchmarking — we want to measure 95th token latency and cost/unit for chat workloads at bursty QPS. can we run a perf lab with dedicated baseline and quant variants?
06:46 Speaker 1 (Jasmine): yes — propose a 2-hour lab with three scenarios: baseline fp16, quantized int4, and mixed routing. we'll collect latency percentiles, token costs, and early quality diffs. Marco will run the lab.
06:58 Speaker 4 (Owen): timeline? you said April 6 earlier. that works for our team.
07:04 Speaker 1 (Jasmine): ok scheduled. Marco to pull a calendar invite.
07:10 Speaker 2 (Nadia): last question — in the listing metadata we have to provide data residency options. we need EU-only hosting for some customers. do you support region-scoped listings?
07:22 Speaker 3 (Marco): yes, listing metadata supports region pinning and we have EU-hosted control plane options; for private BYOK we can run fully in-customer EU region.
07:34 Speaker 7 (Priya): i'll add region checkboxes to the checklist we share.
07:40 Speaker 1 (Jasmine): alright let's recap quickly — action items: Marco runbook by 3/22, Sofia validate KMS policy by 3/19, Owen provide request distribution by 3/20, Jasmine send pricing/metadata by 3/18. we'll follow up with the secure doc links and sample helm chart.
07:58 Speaker 2 (Nadia): thanks all, this was helpful. we'll review the runbook and reconvene after the perf lab.
08:06 Meeting end.

References mentioned: marketplace packaging sample repo: https://redwood.example.com/partner-packaging-sample, runbook template link: https://redwood.example.com/vpc-runbook, SLA doc: shared via secure link.

Notes about transcript: transcription has occasional mislabels and timestamps approximate; filler words preserved.
